The Amazon rainforest might be closer to a tipping point than scientists thought

go.nature.com/4zxEO9I
posts.external_title: A ‘super’ El Niño could transform the Amazon. Is the world’s biggest rainforest doomed?
posts.external_description: Nature - The Amazon rainforest might be closer to a tipping point than scientists thought. Some fear that droughts and fire could nudge it into irreversible decline.

posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: Around 14–15 million years ago, during a cool, arid period, forests in Northwest Africa turned into C3 grasslands, according to a study of plant waxes. The modern savanna, dominated by grasses using the C4 photosystem, appeared in the late Miocene. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/ATpF50ZzW7t

Rapid and prolonged greenhouse warming during the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum caused forests to thin, drastically reshaped plant communities, and reduced overall vegetation carbon storage. 

The results in Science could foreshadow challenges facing modern forests. https://scim.ag/4g8uUST
posts.external_title: Forest canopy decline under elevated CO2 during the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum
posts.external_description: Uncertainty remains regarding the impact of rapid anthropogenic warming on forest ecosystem structure, biodiversity, and function. As an analog, we reconstruct forest canopy density and compositional ...

posts.text: Two scientists working on Italy’s bid to host the Einstein Telescope, Europe’s next-generation gravitational-wave observatory, had their cars set ablaze in Lula, the village in Sardinia where the project would be built. https://scim.ag/4hywK1U
posts.external_title: Arson attack jolts Italy’s bid to host the Einstein Telescope
posts.external_description: Two scientists' cars were burned at the proposed Sardinian site, in what researchers say was an attempt to intimidate supporters of the gravitational-wave observatory

Nature research paper: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance

go.nature.com/4i5VxKH
posts.external_title: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance - Nature
posts.external_description: Substantial intraspecific variation, together with species turnover, drives coordinated shifts in drought resistance such as increased embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins in drier forests.
